forgexSolutions.name: Revenue Leak Check
forgexSolutions.description: One-week audit ($500 fixed price, credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days) to measure how many calls, web-form leads, and quotes slip through and quantify their value.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential delay or drop-off between WordPress web-form inquiries, missed calls while on job sites, and booked jobs.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Field-service software only tracks leads that make it into the system; it does not audit unlogged phone calls, abandoned web forms, or cross-channel response delays.

forgexSolutions.name: Lead-to-job pipeline
forgexSolutions.description: Automated pipeline ($1,800 setup plus $149/month) ensuring every lead from the WordPress forms and other lead sources lands in the field-service software within two minutes, triggers an instant reply (in English or Spanish), and enforces callback reminders.
forgexSolutions.problem: Manual re-keying of Elementor POST form submissions and delayed response to urgent plumbing leads.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: If the company prefers keeping its custom Elementor forms and multi-source lead capture rather than replacing them with a stock iframe widget, custom integration is needed to push leads into the field-service system and trigger immediate multi-step follow-up.

forgexSolutions.name: Owner's Monday numbers
forgexSolutions.description: Weekly one-page summary ($1,200 setup plus $99/month) combining field-service software, accounting, and ad account data into booked revenue, close rate, average ticket, cost per booked job by lead source, and money owed.
forgexSolutions.problem: Lack of unified visibility into true cost per booked job across marketing channels and accounting.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Standard field-service dashboards do not automatically reconcile ad spend and accounting receivables into a single weekly owner scorecard.

feasibility.explanation: Connecting WordPress Elementor forms, phone/call logs, and major field-service management platforms via webhooks and APIs is straightforward and well-supported.

aiDelivery.explanation: Deterministic workflow automation should handle lead routing, CRM/field-service record creation, and KPI calculations, while AI agents can assist with classifying free-text form messages (e.g., distinguishing 24/7 emergencies from routine estimates) and drafting bilingual replies.

humanReview: Owner or dispatcher confirmation before dispatching a plumber or committing to a specific arrival window for 24/7 emergency requests.
Human review of any pricing estimates or non-standard troubleshooting advice before sending to a homeowner.
Owner verification of lead-source attribution mappings during setup of the Owner's Monday numbers report.

risks.description: In 24/7 emergency plumbing (such as burst pipes or sewer backups), an automated reply must never imply a technician is already en route unless confirmed by a human, as delays can result in severe property water damage.
Automated SMS or voice follow-ups triggered from web forms or missed calls must comply with TCPA opt-in and disclosure requirements.
Homeowner personally identifiable information (names, physical addresses, phone numbers, emails) must be transmitted securely over encrypted connections with least-privilege API keys.

commercial.value: Illustrative gross revenue of $800 to $1,500+ per additional water heater installation recovered, or $9,600 to $18,000+ annually if 1 additional installation per month is captured.
commercial.implementationCost: $500 fixed price for the initial Revenue Leak Check (credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days); $1,800 setup plus $149/month for the Lead-to-job pipeline; or $1,200 setup plus $99/month for Owner's Monday numbers.
assumptions: The website states on https://crossflowplumbingllc.com/water-heater-repair-boise/ that 'a new tank water heater is usually starting at $800 installed and tankless is $1,500 and up.'
Illustrative assumption: faster automated lead capture and instant reply recovers 1 previously missed water heater installation lead per month (12 per year).

Illustrative calculation: 1 job/month x $800 starting tank price = $800/month ($9,600/year), or 1 job/month x $1,500 starting tankless price = $1,500/month ($18,000/year) in gross revenue before labor and equipment costs.

discovery.outreachSubject: Question about Crossflow Plumbing's web form leads & after-hours calls
discovery.outreachBody:
Hi [redacted],

I was looking through crossflowplumbingllc.com and saw how you've built Crossflow Plumbing around fast 1-2 hour emergency response and upfront pricing across Eagle and the Treasure Valley.

I noticed your site uses standard contact forms alongside your Housecall Pro reviews widget. When you and the team are under a house or handling after-hours calls, do web form inquiries and missed calls go straight into your dispatch software with an instant reply, or does someone have to enter and follow up on them manually?

At ForgeX, we offer a fixed-price Revenue Leak Check ($500, credited in full toward any fix you order within 30 days). limitations: Employee headcount is not stated on the website; while the site refers to 'our plumbers' and 'our team', it cannot be confirmed from public pages whether the company employs 10 to 75 staff or is a smaller crew.
Whether the company pays for leads (e.g., paid search or lead-generation networks) cannot be confirmed from the website alone, although Google Tag (GT-K52TXMCT) is installed.
No specific Idaho state plumbing contractor license number is listed on the website.
Backend form routing (whether the WordPress POST forms trigger a webhook into Housecall Pro or simply send an email) is not observable from public page source.

qualification.rationale: Crossflow Plumbing LLC is an owner-led residential plumbing contractor in Eagle, Idaho with a clear decision-maker (Owner [redacted]), a verified business contact channel ([redacted]), and observable evidence of using WordPress/Elementor POST forms alongside a client.housecallpro.com widget. However, because employee headcount (target 10-75 staff), paid lead spend, and whether web-form leads are handled manually or already automated in the backend are unconfirmed hypotheses rather than verified facts, 'pursue later' is the appropriate qualification.
